utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: I’m in, but we should map out the timing and who’s bringing what first so nothing gets missed.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Good call, Pia — I can grab the drill, extension cord, and a couple of screwdrivers. If you make the timing list, I’ll match it with the tools and set-up we need.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Perfect — I’ll sketch the timing list and a quick supplies checklist, then we can compare notes before we head over.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: Sounds good — I’ll work the repair drive around the school schedule, and we can keep it as simple as possible.

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: Thanks, Faye. I appreciate you keeping it simple — that helps a lot.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: Of course — I’ll check the school calendar first and then line up the repair drive around that. I’ll keep you posted once I’ve got a workable time.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Sounds good — I’m in. Just point me to what needs fixing and I’ll help where I can.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Thanks, Bo — I’ll check with the others and send you the list once I get the latest update.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Perfect — send it over when you have it, and I’ll jump on the easy fixes first.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Got it — I’ll keep it short and practical. What do you need done for the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Thanks, Leo — we need a quick hand sorting the donated tools and making sure the labels match the bins. If you can help with that, it’ll keep the repair drive running smoothly.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Sure — I can sort the tools and match the labels to the bins. Just point me to the table and I’ll get started.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: I can help with the repair drive—just tell me what needs fixing first.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Thanks, Rey — first up is the loose porch step and that leaky faucet by the shed. If you’re still around later, I’d really appreciate the extra hands.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: I’m around, so I can take those on. Want me to start with the porch step or the faucet?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Could you share the repair drive details one more time? I want to make sure I’ve got everything right before I help.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Sure — I can share them again, but I don’t have the repair drive details written down yet. If you send me the list, I’ll help keep track of it.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Thanks, Cleo — I don’t have the list either, so let’s pause until someone sends the repair drive details.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Oh—right, the repair drive. I’m happy to help out; just point me to what needs doing and I’ll get on it.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Thanks, Oren! I’ll swing by with the repair list and a few tools, and we can start with the porch lights and that loose fence panel.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Sounds good—bring the list and I’ll be ready. I might need you to remind me which light was the porch one, but I’ll do my best!

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: I’m happy to help with the repair drive—what do you need me to take on?

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: That’s wonderful, Mara — could you help by coordinating volunteer sign-ups and keeping track of what supplies we still need?

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Absolutely — I can coordinate the volunteer sign-ups and keep a running list of needed supplies. I’ll check in and let you know what’s missing.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: I haven’t tracked any repair-drive locations yet, but I can help keep an eye on them if you want.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Could you start tracking them and tell me the first few spots you find?

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Absolutely — I’ll start tracking the repair-drive spots and note the first few I find. I’ll report back as soon as I’ve got them.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Sounds good — I’ll keep an ear out while I’m out running errands.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Thanks, Ira — I appreciate it. I’ll keep coordinating the repair drive and let you know if anything changes.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: No problem — I’ll ask around and see if anyone needs a hand. If I hear anything useful, I’ll pass it along.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh—right, the repair drive. I’m a bit scattered today, but I can help if you tell me what changed.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Can you confirm whether the drive is still on for today, or did something change?

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: I’m not sure yet — I haven’t heard about any change, so I’d assume it’s still on for today until someone says otherwise.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Absolutely — happy to help with the repair drive. What do you need from me?

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Thanks, Sam. I’d like to keep it simple: first we’ll sort the tools, then I’ll write up the list, and after that we can load the truck together.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Sounds good — I can sort the tools and help load the truck when you’re ready.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Morning, Pia. Let’s keep it simple: first we sort the parts, then we load the tools, and after that we head out for the repair drive.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Sounds good, but I’d like to double-check the parts list before we load anything so we don’t miss a thing.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: That’s sensible. Let’s check the parts list together first, then we’ll load the tools once everything’s confirmed.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Oh, I heard the repair drive is moving along nicely—folks are bringing in tools and parts already. If you want, I can swing by and see what they still need.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Are you sure it’s moving along nicely, Ira? I’d feel better if we knew exactly what they still need before you go over there.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: You’re right—I shouldn’t guess. I’ll ask them first and come back with a clear list of what they need.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Sounds good — what do you need me to bring for the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Could you bring packing tape, zip ties, and a box of basic screws? If you’ve got a flashlight too, that’d be great.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Got it — I’ll bring the tape, zip ties, basic screws, and a flashlight if I can find one.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Absolutely, Leo — I’m getting the repair drive organized and I’ll keep things moving. Let’s make a quick list of what needs fixing first.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Sounds good — let’s start with the biggest fixes first, then we can work down the list.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Great — I’ll note the biggest fixes first, and then we can add the smaller ones underneath. What’s at the top of your list?

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Absolutely — I’m happy to help with the repair drive. What do you need from me?

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Thanks, Sam — could you help sort the donated items and keep a quick tally of what comes in? I’ll handle the sign-in sheet and labels.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Of course — I’ll sort the donated items and keep a running tally as they come in. Just point me to the table and I’ll get started.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: I’ll spread the word about the repair drive right away—who should I invite first?

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: Start with the folks on Maple and anyone who’s mentioned a broken fence or squeaky door. I can help you make a quick list if you want.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Perfect — I’ll start with Maple and the neighbors who need fixes, then we can add anyone else nearby. Let’s make that quick list together.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: I don’t have any repair-drive locations noted yet, Nell. If you want, I can keep track of the drop-off spot and any nearby details for you.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: That’d help a lot, Opal — I’ll let you know the drop-off spot and any nearby details as soon as I hear them.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Perfect — send me the drop-off spot and any nearby landmarks when you get them, and I’ll keep it all straight for us.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Oh, right—the repair drive. I’m happy to help, if you remind me what still needs doing.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Thanks, Oren — we still need someone to sort the tools, set out the sign-up sheet, and help unload donations when they arrive. If you can take one of those, that’d be a big help.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: I can take the sign-up sheet—just point me to where you want it set out, and I’ll handle that.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: I can help keep folks in the loop on the repair drive—want me to coordinate updates or spread the word to different groups?

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Yeah, that’d help a lot—maybe you can handle the updates, and I’ll try to spread the word around too.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Absolutely — I’ll handle the updates and keep everyone posted, and you can keep spreading the word on your end. Let’s check in after we’ve both talked to a few folks.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: I heard the repair drive’s getting a decent turnout already—people are bringing tools, paint, and a few extra hands. If you’re heading over, I can tell you what they still need.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Sounds good—tell me what they still need, and I’ll see if I can bring something useful.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: They could still use drop cloths, extension cords, and a couple of screwdrivers if you’ve got them. Oh, and bottled water never hurts—folks are working up a sweat already.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Could you tell me the details of the repair drive first—what needs fixing and when it’s happening?

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Sure — what exactly needs repair, and what date are you planning for it?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Thanks — I’m still checking the specifics, so I’ll confirm what needs fixing and the date before I say more.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: I can help with the repair drive—what do you need me to bring or fix?

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Thanks, Leo — could you bring a drill, a hammer, and any spare screws you have? If you’ve got time, we could also use help patching a loose fence panel.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Yep — I can bring the drill, hammer, and some screws, and I can help patch the fence panel too.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh, hey Rosa — sorry, I missed that. What’s the repair drive about?

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: No worries, Noah — the repair drive is just our neighborhood day for fixing small things together, like bikes, chairs, and little home repairs. If you’ve got something that needs a quick fix, bring it by and we’ll take a look.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh, that sounds handy — I’ve got a wobbly chair that could use a look. What time should I bring it by?

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: I can help coordinate around the school schedule if you need me to. What time is the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Thanks, Faye — it starts at 9:00 a.m. Could you help me work around the school pickup time?

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: Absolutely — I can help with that. School pickup is usually around 3:00 p.m., so we have some flexibility before then.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Could you share the repair drive details again so I can check everything carefully before we go ahead?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Of course — I can resend the repair drive details right away, and I’ll make sure everything is clear and easy to check. If you want, I can also summarize the key points here in one quick message.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Thanks, Jules — please send the full details, and a quick summary would help too so I can verify everything carefully.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: I haven’t tracked the repair drive yet, Gus—where should I note the location?

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Jot it down at the community shed by the notice board, Opal — that’s where we’re keeping the repair drive sign-in.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Got it — I’ll note it at the community shed by the notice board.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: I heard the repair drive’s getting a good turnout—people are dropping things off all morning. I’ll swing by later and see if they need any extra hands.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Oh, that’s great to hear. If you find out they need help, let me know—I’m happy to pitch in too.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Will do — I’m heading that way after I finish a couple errands, and I’ll let you know if they need more hands.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Oh, right — the repair drive! I’m a bit rusty on the details, but I’m happy to help out however I can.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Thanks, Oren — that helps a lot. I’ll send over the repair drive details and a couple of easy ways you can pitch in.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: That sounds perfect, Sam — send it over when you can and I’ll do my best to jump in where needed.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh, the repair drive? I heard they’re looking for a few more volunteers this weekend, and there’s already a nice pile of donations coming in.

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: That’s good to hear—I'll check what supplies we still need and bring anything I can. If they need a hand sorting donations, I can do that too.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: That’d be wonderful, Cleo! I’ll ask around and see whether they still need help sorting, and I’ll let you know what supplies are missing.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: I’m thinking we should map out the repair drive first, then I’ll pass the plan along to everyone. If you’re in, I can help organize the next steps.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Sounds reasonable, but can you confirm what you mean by the repair drive and who’s being included?

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: I mean a neighborhood repair drive for shared fixes like the fence, walkway, and any small household repairs folks want help with. I’d include anyone nearby who wants to join, and I can send the plan around once we settle the list.

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: I can help a little, but I need to keep things low-key right now.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: That’s okay, Uli — low-key is fine. Just tell me what you can take on, and I’ll work around it.

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: I can do a small amount of sorting and maybe one quiet errand, but I can’t stay long. If you leave me a simple list, I’ll handle what I can.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Hey Bo, sorry I’m late—what’s the latest on the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: No worries — looks like we’re still collecting the big items, and I’m keeping it moving as best I can. If you’ve got anything to add, send it my way.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Got it — I’ll check around and see if anyone else has big items to add, then I’ll send them your way.
